about: Decoder caps. XRPL: STObject and STArray fields nest at most 64 levels inside a transaction (an object or array field one level below its container, an array's member object one level below the array); the blobs were written by ripple-binary-codec 2.11.0's encode, each a Payment whose depth is by construction. The cap is checked in one pass over the blob's fields before the codec decodes it, so XC5, the largest blob decodeBlob takes (4096 hex characters) nesting to level 1010, is refused in time linear in its length. msgpack: arrays and maps nest at most 32 levels, the outermost container being level 1, every declared length is at most the bytes left, and the bytes are exactly one value; the scan does not judge a string's bytes, a key or a format, which the Algorand reader reads as each member's type is read; each row is hand-written from the msgpack specification's formats, and Python 3.12.3's strict UTF-8 codec refuses the string of each row whose case says it is not well-formed. ScVal: vectors and maps (a contract instance's storage counting as a map) nest at most 64 levels within one ScVal, the outermost container being level 1; each ScVal is hand-written XDR (RFC 4506). Authorized invocations nest at most 64 levels within one authorization entry, the root invocation being level 1. In an envelope the cap applies to what decodeStellarTx reads, the operation and the payer's authorization entry; every other part (another entry, a delegate, the footprint, another operation, a claim predicate) is not walked and is decoded whatever its depth. The envelopes are x402-exact-stellar.json V2's signed envelope edited with @stellar/stellar-sdk 17.2.1's XDR types: SE1 and SE2 wrap the payer's signature (a vector of one map, 2 levels) in vectors, SE3 and SE4 add a second authorization entry under the source account's credentials, SE5 gives the payer's transfer a chain of sub-invocations, SE6 gives the operation a fourth argument, SE7 adds a second authorization entry under address credentials with delegates (the account key of 32 bytes of 04, a void signature, and x(void) on the contract of 32 bytes of 06 as its invocation) whose delegates nest 66 deep, and SE8 replaces the operation with a create-claimable-balance of 1 stroop of the native asset whose one claimant (the account key of 32 bytes of 05) has a predicate nesting 66 deep, 65 not-predicates around an unconditional one. SE9 to SE75 hold each recursive shape at 64 and 65 levels in each place it can sit, and in each place lcp does not read, at the least level js-xdr 5.0.0's default depth (1,500) refuses where that fits in 8,192 characters, as each row's case says. The places are the payer's signature (replaced), a fourth argument of the operation, the payer's invocations, a second entry as SE3's (its argument or invocations), as SE7's (its one delegate's signature, or its delegates) or under the address credentials of the account key of 32 bytes of 08 with a void signature (its signature or invocations), a footprint of one read-only persistent contract-data key on the contract of 32 bytes of 07, a second operation (x(value) on the contract of 32 bytes of 06, or a create-claimable-balance as SE8's), and SE8's operation. Each map and contract instance storage holds one entry whose key is void, each contract instance's executable is the Stellar asset, and each and-predicate's first operand is unconditional. Past the cap in what is read is refused; every other row reads as V2's envelope reads without its nesting. A row's expect, where it has one, is decodeStellarTx's refusal. 'accept' says whether the caps admit the input.
